newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian farmers welcome APEC declaration.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian farmers welcome APEC declaration.

text.p: Australia's National Farmers' Federation (NFF) said on Wednesday the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) Group's trade declaration would prompt further liberalisation of multilateral trade.
In the declaration, the 18 APEC nations pledged to push for the elimination of information technology sector tariffs and to identify other areas for the removal of tariffs next year.

"While we are disappointed that there were no major commitments to the reduction of tariff levels in agriculture, NFF welcomes the progress made in the area of non-tariff barriers," NFF president Donald McGauchie said in a statement.

"Of particular note were commitments from Japan to review their quarantine arrangements, to facilitate the entry of plant and animal imports -- a clear acknowledgement from Japan that agriculture is an important part of the APEC proces and a potential boost to Australian horticulture."

McGauchie said other positive developments were Thailand's commitment to increase its quotas in skim milk powder and soybean products, and Canada's elimination of export subsidies on grain and oilseeds.
The annual APEC leaders' meeting finished on Monday in Manila.

APEC comprises Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
